summary: Tested the record-level concurrency store (backend + UI). test_concurrency.py passes 12/12, before and after my fix. A new edge suite (test_record_store_edge.py) found that a stock 'inc' was lost when it was in the same batch as an upsert of that item. I fixed it in record_store.py and the suite now passes 5/5. UI tests with 5 concurrent browser sessions (admin x3, aaa x2) creating GRNs at the same moment worked: all 5 GRNs were kept with unique numbers (GRN-2026-380..384, colliding numbers renumbered automatically), every tab showed all 5 within 16s and after reload, there were exactly 5 activity logs and 5 grnAudit entries, and stock rose by exactly 5. Same-GRN edit conflict (saves less than 1s apart) worked: the Conflict panel listed field / original / mine / theirs, 'Reload latest' showed the other user's value with the indicator back to Saved, and 'Re-apply' saved my value on top. Simultaneous GRN create (stock +1) and GRN delete (stock -1) on the same item ended at the exact stock. Offline save worked: unsaved -> saving -> failed with a Retry banner, no premature 'Saved', saved exactly once after going online. Session expiry worked in the simple case: 'Session expired' banner, Log in again, the change was re-sent once. Regression smoke: 13 pages load, Monthly P&L manual value persists after reload (reverted). Found 3 CRITICAL silent-overwrite / data-loss bugs and several medium ones, listed below. All test data was cleaned up: stock restored to 383, PO-2026-322 is back to Approved, GRNs, audit entries and logs were deleted by id.

critical.issue: FIXED BY TESTER: if a batch held an 'inc' and an 'upsert' for the same item (computeOps puts inc first, e.g. an Item Master edit that changes Current Stock and any other field), the upsert re-set currentStock from the pre-batch snapshot and the increment was lost. Fix: re-read the record before keeping currentStock. Covered by test_record_store_edge.py::test_inc_and_upsert_same_item_same_batch.

minor.issue: Serialisation relies on a per-process asyncio.Lock, and on transactions only if Mongo is a replica set. With more than one uvicorn worker or pod, revision checks are not atomic. Without transactions, an exception partway through _apply leaves partial writes and no erp_applied row, so a retry would apply 'inc' ops twice.
An 'inc' on a missing or deleted record id is silently ignored and still returns 200.
erp_applied grows without limit (no TTL index), and soft-deleted records are never purged.

purchase/purchase123 (and purchase@amrest.in/purchase123) return 401. The credentials file is wrong, or the user does not exist. Testing and production users have no GRN permission, so the 5-session GRN test used admin x3 + aaa@amrest.in x2.

ui_bugs.component: All edit modals (GRN edit, Item Master edit, PO edit, ...) + lib/sync.ts applyChanges
ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL SILENT OVERWRITE, reproduced in the UI. A opens the GRN edit modal; B edits Invoice# of the same GRN and saves; within 10s A's tab pulls, and because the record is untouched in A's db, its base and rev move to B's version; A then changes Invoice Amount and saves. A's stale form (spread from ...editGRN) is sent with the NEW baseRev, so the server accepts it, B's Invoice# is silently reverted, and no Conflict panel appears. The Conflict panel only shows when both saves land within the 10s pull window.

ui_bugs.component: Item Master edit (pages/Items.tsx save) + computeOps items inc
ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL STOCK OVERWRITE, reproduced. A opens Edit Item (stock 390); B creates a GRN (+1, server 391); A's tab pulls; A changes Sale Rate and clicks Update. The form still carries currentStock 390, computeOps sends inc -1, and B's GRN stock is silently reverted (final 390, expected 391).

ui_bugs.component: lib/store.tsx flushSave conflict/duplicate branch for replayed batches (re-login / reload)
ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL DATA LOSS, reproduced. A's session expires and A creates a GRN (kept unsaved). B creates a GRN with the same next number. A logs in again; the replayed batch gets 409 duplicates. renumber(dbRef.current) cannot find the record because hydrate replaced dbRef with server state (the record only exists in inflight.ops), pendingOps() is then empty, the indicator shows 'Saved', and localStorage unsaved ops are cleared. A's GRN and its stock +1 are permanently lost. A replayed batch that hits a real conflict has the same problem: mine is undefined and Re-apply drops it.

integration_issues.issue: Only the conflicting records are reverted. Side records created in the same rejected batch (Activity Log entry and grnAudit 'Edited Invoiceno. -> TEST_B1') are still re-sent and saved, so Activity Log and GRN audit record a change that was discarded. After 'Re-apply', the audit text shows the stale 'from' value (TEST_A1 -> TEST_B2 instead of TEST_A2 -> TEST_B2).

After a successful replay, the tab does not show its own re-sent change (the GRN is not in the list and stock is not updated) until a full reload. baseRef = snapshot (the server state from before the replay) and version.current = res.version, so pull() never fetches it.

integration_issues.flow: Daily Production Entry (code review, not UI-tested)
integration_issues.issue: Each entry also upserts the jobCards record (stage status, date, worker) and can upsert serials, so two operators entering on the same Job Card at the same time will get the Conflict panel. API-level concurrent production entries pass.

issues: React warning: <span> cannot be a child of <option> (hydration error)
Charts: <rect> negative height warnings on Dashboard/Reports
401 resource errors logged around the login flow

action_items: CRITICAL: Pin the base revision when an edit starts, not when it is saved. Suggestion: server writes data._rev (or the client stamps the rev into each record on load and pull), and computeOps uses the local record's own _rev as baseRev, so a stale form spread from an old object always gets a 409 and the Conflict panel.

CRITICAL: Item Master save (and any form that spreads a stale item) must not send stale currentStock. Apply only the user's intended delta (form.currentStock - edit.currentStock) on top of the current item, or exclude currentStock unless the user changed it.

CRITICAL: On replay after login or reload, apply the saved ops to the freshly hydrated local state, so records exist in dbRef for renumber and conflict resolution. Never mark 'saved' or clear the unsaved ops while a rejected replay batch is unresolved. Then pull/refetch so the tab shows the replayed change.
Conflict 'Reload latest' must also drop the logs and grnAudit entries created by the rejected batch. 'Re-apply' should regenerate the audit text against the latest values.
Fix the credentials doc / user for purchase/purchase123.
Consider an erp_applied TTL index, returning 4xx for inc on a missing record, and documenting the single-worker requirement (or using a Mongo replica set and transactions).
critical_code_review_comments: record_store._apply: cur[] snapshot is taken before any writes, so any op that reads prev after an earlier op in the same batch touched the record is stale. The items currentStock case is fixed; check the same pattern for purchaseOrders status derivation.

sync.applyChanges advances base and rev for any record not modified in the global db. Modal drafts live in component state, so the server cannot see that they are stale. This is the root of the silent-overwrite bug.
store.flushSave duplicate branch: renumber() works on dbRef only; replayed inflight ops (from localStorage) are not represented in dbRef.
Item Master 'Current Stock' is editable in the edit form and turns into an inc delta. Concurrent GRNs make this delta wrong unless it is computed relative to the value when the modal was opened.
read_state streams every record on each load; acceptable now, but watch payload size.

Repro for silent overwrite: keep the edit modal open for more than 12s while another session saves the same record.
rca of the issue: 1) Silent overwrite: the pull loop (every 10s) treats a record as 'not being edited' when the global db copy equals base, but edit modals hold a detached copy. The base rev moves forward, so the stale draft is saved with the fresh rev. Mitigation: the rev must travel with the record copy (data._rev) or be pinned when the edit begins. 2) Stock revert: Items.tsx saves the whole form, including stale currentStock, and computeOps turns the difference into an inc. 3) Replay data loss: hydrateFromServer sets dbRef to server state and inflight.ops is the only holder of the change. The duplicate and conflict handlers look only in dbRef, so the change is dropped and the UI shows Saved.
